payload.title: The baseline exam reads runs.jsonl through read_runs_rows, which only parses JSON lines, and never verifies the ledger's hash chain, so a hand-edited ledger (status, snapshot flags, findings pointers changed) is accepted and stamped as a measurement of the kept store
evidence: tools/aria-acceptance/harness.py:722 (the exam reads runs.jsonl with read_runs_rows)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/runs_reader.py:38-57 (read_runs_rows: strict JSON parse and upcast, no chain check)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/ledger.py:2148-2167 (load_jsonl_verified: the verified loader; its docstring names the runs-loader among the hot-path consumers that must use it)
tools/aria-acceptance/harness.py:383 (the same harness verifies cycles.jsonl with load_jsonl_verified)
payload.rule_violated: Append-only integrity (Plan 026R A.2): a reader whose output is stamped as evidence must load the ledger through load_jsonl_verified so a tamper surfaces as a failure.
payload.notes: An operator or a process edits a row of a kept store's runs.jsonl (flips a status, sets dirty_snapshot, changes an artifact pointer) without recomputing the chain. load_jsonl_verified raises ledger_hash_mismatch on that file, but the exam parses each line as JSON and carries on, so the report is stamped with the real ARIA SHA and corpus hash and --against calls it reproduced. The stamp then vouches for numbers the store's own integrity check rejects. The trigger needs a hand-edited ledger, which is exactly the case the chain exists for; the kernel's own read_runs_for_cycle shares the strict-JSON-only read, so the close here is local to the exam. Close condition: Verify the plain runs.jsonl with ledger.load_jsonl_verified (read only, no diagnostics) before reading it and refuse by name on a mismatch. Add a test that flips one byte of a row in a store copy and asserts a named refusal, exit 2, and no --out. Verified at origin/main ae2958653d.
